scientific_question: On a real pretrained, architecturally different foundation model (SkySense++ S2, semantic-enhanced 24-layer ViT-L), does ICE deliver a certified exact efficiency gain under a matched intermediate-feature receiver, and is the gain receiver-determined rather than forced?

setup.backbone: SkySense++ S2 ViT-L (302.6M, 24-layer pre-LN, semantic-enhanced merge_stage=4, real pretrained weights via BiliSakura HF Apache-2.0 conversion of skysensepp_release_s2.pth)
setup.data: SEN12TS WorldCover 11-class, 120x120, train 840 / val 180, frozen micro_batch 16 per-batch dynamic normalization on the 10-band S2 subset
setup.training: frozen backbone + trainable conv1x1 head only, CE+Lovasz 1:1, AdamW, 24 epochs, seed 0, AMP validation
setup.annotation: GT WorldCover labels as semantic-vocabulary indices (leakage documented) or empty constant-zero map (control)

contracts.A_full_depth_control: receiver reads official outputs at layers 5/11/17/23 (mirrors official UPerNet-style usage)
contracts.B_matched_intermediate: receiver reads layer 11 only; ICE executes layers 0-11, eliminates 12-23 (12/24 layers)

preregistered_gates.gate1_exactness: 100% validation prediction agreement + retained feature maps FP32 + logits FP32 + gradients + confusion matrix (hard)
preregistered_gates.gate3_export: physical parameter removal with whole-validation prediction identity

contract_A_gt.role: full-depth control - ICE correctly finds no removable compute when the receiver reads the final layer

contract_A_empty.role: leakage control for A (GT leakage contribution ~16.9pp at full depth)

contract_B_gt.role: matched intermediate receiver (layer 11) - the second positive backbone result

contract_B_empty.role: leakage control for B (GT leakage contribution ~7.9pp at layer 11); proves exactness/latency are independent of mIoU and annotation

conclusions.second_positive_backbone: Confirmed. SkySense++ S2 (24-layer semantic-enhanced, architecturally distinct from CROMA's dual-tower 12-layer + cross-encoder) delivers 38.7% latency reduction (batch16) / 41.9% (batch1) with 100% prediction identity, 49.9% physical parameter removal, all under a matched intermediate-feature receiver with real pretrained weights.
conclusions.receiver_determined_not_forced: The A/B contract pair on the same backbone and same weights gives 0% vs 38.7% latency reduction - ICE savings are determined by the downstream receiver contract, not imposed by ICE. Contract A (official full-depth usage) correctly returns ~0% removable compute (fail-closed).
conclusions.leakage_quantified: GT annotation contributes ~7.9pp (B) to ~16.9pp (A) over the empty control, but the empty control still reaches 12.9-13.9% (above the ~9% random baseline), and - critically - ICE exactness and latency reduction are unchanged between GT and empty runs, proving they are pure structural properties.

cross_backbone_evidence.AnySat: 0% removable under its official dense contract (fail-closed boundary, R22)
cross_backbone_evidence.statement: Two independent real pretrained positive backbones of different architectures plus one fail-closed boundary establish ICE as a dependency compiler whose savings are determined by (receiver contract x backbone graph), generalizing beyond any single model.

caveats.annotation_leakage: GT annotation is fed to the semantic-enhanced backbone (its native input contract); mIoU numbers are GT-guided and not comparable to leakage-free segmentation; the empty control quantifies the leakage contribution.
caveats.resolution: 120x120 input (pos_embed bicubic-resized from the 16x16 pretraining grid) - reported as a known boundary.
caveats.mIoU_levels: Absolute mIoU (20.85% B-GT) is below the CROMA baseline (49.8%) because the 1x1 head on frozen features is a linear probe, not a tuned decoder; R24's scientific claim is ICE exactness/efficiency, not mIoU superiority.
caveats.weights_origin: Official SkySense++ weights are distributed via a dead Notion link; the BiliSakura HF conversion (Apache-2.0) of skysensepp_release_s2.pth was used (missing=0/unexpected=0).
